{{nihongo|'''Ninomiya Shrine'''|二宮神社 (三宅村)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

It stands directly in front of Tsubota fishing port in the southeast of Miyake-jima.

Several {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and many nearby small shrines are merged here, centered on '''Iwanohime-no-Mikoto Shrine''' (いわのひめのみことじんじゃ)<ref name="kanko">[https://www.miyakejima.gr.jp/see/ninomiya_shrine/ 二宮神社] - Miyakejima Tourism Association</ref><ref name="chosa">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140118-02.html 二宮神社] - Research on Engishiki Shrines</ref><ref name="miyake-84">[https://www.soumu.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/14miyake/miyakehp/kankousasshi_0503.pdf Miyakejima p.84 (Shikinaisha of Miyakejima)] - Tokyo Metropolitan Government / Miyakejima Tourism Association</ref>.

It is one of three shrines on Miyake-jima that enshrine the consort of {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}} (Mishima Daimyōjin)<ref>[https://www.vill.miyake.tokyo.jp/gyousei/syoukai/history.html History] - Miyakejima, Tokyo</ref>.

=== History ===
The central Iwanohime-no-Mikoto Shrine originally stood in the northern mountains of the current site (present Iwaha Kannon Shrine / Tsubota Kannon), then in the early Kamakura period moved to southwest of the current site, south of Ōji-ike (Ogura-yama, with torii still extant). Later, in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 29 ({{ill|1954|ab|1954|ace|1954|af|1954|als|1954|am|1954 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1954|ar|1954|ary|1954|arz|1954|ast|1954|av|1954 сон|avk|1954|az|1954|azb|۱۹۵۴ (میلادی)|ba|1954 йыл|ban|1954|bat_smg|1954|bcl|1954|be|1954|be_x_old|1954|bg|1954|bh|1954|bjn|1954|bn|১৯৫৪|bpy|মারি ১৯৫৪|br|1954|bs|1954.|ca|1954|cbk_zam|1954|cdo|1954 nièng|ce|1954 шо|ceb|1954|ckb|١٩٥٤|co|1954|crh|1954|cs|1954|csb|1954|cv|1954|cy|1954|da|1954|de|1954|diq|1954|dsb|1954|el|1954|eml|1954|eo|1954|es|1954|et|1954|eu|1954|fa|۱۹۵۴|fi|1954|fiu_vro|1954|fo|1954|fr|1954|frp|1954|frr|1954|fur|1954|fy|1954|ga|1954|gag|1954|gan|1954年|gcr|1954|gd|1954|gl|1954|gn|1954|gv|1954|hak|1954-ngièn|he|1954|hi|१९५४|hif|1954|hr|1954.|hsb|1954|ht|1954 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1954|hy|1954|hyw|1954 թուական|ia|1954|id|1954|ie|1954|ilo|1954|inh|1954 шу|io|1954|is|1954|it|1954|ja|1954年|jbo|1954moi|jv|1954|ka|1954|kaa|1954|kab|1954|kbp|1954|kk|1954 жыл|kn|೧೯೫೪|ko|1954년|krc|1954 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1954|ku|1954|kv|1954-ӧд во|kw|1954|la|1954|lb|1954|lez|1954 йис|li|1954|lij|1954|lld|1954|lmo|1954|ln|1954|lt|1954 m.|lv|1954. gads|mai|१९५४|map_bms|1954|mdf|1954|mg|1954|mhr|1954|mi|1954|min|1954|mk|1954|ml|1954|mn|1954 он|mr|इ.स. १९५४|mrj|1954 и|ms|1954|my|၁၉၅၄|myv|1954 ие|mzn|۱۹۵۴|nah|1954|nap|1954|nds|1954|nds_nl|1954|new|ई सं १९५४|nl|1954|nn|1954|no|1954|nrm|1954|nso|1954|oc|1954|olo|1954|or|୧୯୫୪|os|1954-æм аз|pa|1954|pam|1954|pap|1954|pl|1954|pnb|1954|pt|1954|qu|1954|ro|1954|roa_rup|1954|roa_tara|1954|ru|1954 год|rue|1954|sah|1954|sc|1954|scn|1954|sd|1954ع|se|1954|sh|1954.|shn|1954|si|1954|simple|1954|sk|1954|sl|1954|smn|1954|so|1954|sq|1954|sr|1954|stq|1954|su|1954|sv|1954|sw|1954|szl|1954|ta|1954|te|1954|tg|Соли 1954|th|พ.ศ. 2497|tk|1954|tl|1954|tly|1954|tpi|1954|tr|1954|tt|1954 ел|ty|1954|udm|1954 ар|ug|1954 - يىلى|uk|1954|ur|1954ء|uz|1954|vec|1954|vi|1954|vls|1954|vo|1954|wa|1954|war|1954|xmf|1954|yi|1954|za|1954 nienz|zea|1954|zh|1954年|zh_classical|一九五四年|zh_min_nan|1954 nî|zh_yue|1954年|qid=Q18581}}), nearby shrines were consolidated into and merged with {{ill|Sugawara Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|菅原神社|qid=Q48532247}} (of {{ill|Tenjin faith|ja|天神信仰|ko|천신신앙|qid=Q66890725}}), which stood at the current site, and it was renamed Ninomiya Shrine<ref name="chosa"/><ref name="miyake-84"/>.

The name Ninomiya Shrine could be interpreted as deriving from the deity being the second daughter among the Hakone three sisters, but the official explanation says it derives from the second prince who is traditionally said to have accompanied the deity<ref name="kanko"/>.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* Iwanohime-no-Mikoto (いわのひめのみこと) - one of the consort deities of {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}} (Mishima Daimyōjin).

According to the mythology in ''Miyakeki'', the three sister-consorts of Mishima Daimyōjin (Kotoshironushi-no-Kami), enshrined in shrines on Miyake-jima, were daughters of an old couple living around {{ill|Lake Ashi|ar|بحيرة أشي|arz|بحيره اشى|ceb|Ashino Ko|cv|Аси (кӳлĕ)|de|Ashi-See|el|Λίμνη Άσι|es|Lago Ashi|eu|Ashi aintzira|fa|دریاچه هاکونه|fi|Ashi|fr|Lac Ashi|he|אגם אשי|it|Lago Ashi|ja|芦ノ湖|ko|아시노호|mn|Аши нуур|ms|Tasik Ashi|my|အရှိကန်|pt|Lago Ashi|ru|Асиноко|sl|Aši (jezero)|th|ทะเลสาบอาชิ|tr|Ashi Gölü|zh|蘆之湖|qid=Q187053}} in {{ill|Hakone|ja|箱根|qid=Q11603342}}, rescued from a dragon deity (great serpent) and brought to Miyake-jima. The eldest is Igamuhime-no-Mikoto enshrined at {{ill|Kisaki Shrine|ja|后神社 (三宅村)|qid=Q134930558|lt=Kisaki Shrine}}, the second is Iwanohime-no-Mikoto enshrined at Ninomiya Shrine, and the third is Sakitamahime-no-Mikoto enshrined at {{ill|Oshaku Shrine|Q110915859|qid=Q110915859}}<ref name="chosa-miyake">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz149900-01.html Shrines of Miyakejima] - Research on Engishiki Shrines</ref>.
